:::{#thm-hat-matrix-projects}
#### The hat matrix projects onto the column space of the design matrix

If $\mX$ is an $n \times p$ design matrix with $\operatorname{rank}(\mX) = p$,
then for every $\vy \in \reals^n$,
$\matr{H} \vy$ (@def-hat-matrix) is the orthogonal projection of $\vy$ onto $\mathcal{C}(\mX)$.
So $\matr{H} = \matr{Q} \tp{\matr{Q}}$
for any $n \times p$ matrix $\matr{Q}$ whose columns are an orthonormal basis of $\mathcal{C}(\mX)$.

:::

::: proof

$\matr{H}$ is an orthogonal projection matrix (@thm-hat-matrix),
so $\matr{H} \vy$ is the orthogonal projection of $\vy$ onto $\mathcal{C}(\matr{H})$
(@thm-projection-matrix-projects, part 1).
It remains to show $\mathcal{C}(\matr{H}) = \mathcal{C}(\mX)$.

- $\mathcal{C}(\matr{H}) \subseteq \mathcal{C}(\mX)$:
  $\matr{H} \vecf{z} = \mX\,\paren{(\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1} \tp{\mX} \vecf{z}}$ (@thm-matmul-assoc),
  which is in $\mathcal{C}(\mX)$ (@def-column-space).
- $\mathcal{C}(\mX) \subseteq \mathcal{C}(\matr{H})$:
  $\matr{H} \mX = \mX (\tp{\mX}\mX)^{-1} (\tp{\mX}\mX) = \mX$
  (@thm-matmul-assoc, @def-matrix-inverse, @thm-identity),
  so $\mX \vecf{b} = \matr{H}\,(\mX \vecf{b})$ is in $\mathcal{C}(\matr{H})$ for every $\vecf{b}$.

$\mathcal{C}(\mX)$ has dimension $p$ (@thm-rank-dim),
so an orthonormal basis of it has $p$ vectors (@thm-basis-size),
and $\matr{Q} \tp{\matr{Q}}$ also gives the orthogonal projection onto $\mathcal{C}(\mX)$
(@thm-projector-onb).
By @thm-projection-matrix-projects, part 2, $\matr{H} = \matr{Q} \tp{\matr{Q}}$.

:::

{{< slidebreak >}}

:::{#exm-hat-matrix-projects}
#### The intercept-only hat matrix, from an orthonormal basis

For the intercept-only design $\mX = \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix}$ of @exm-hat-matrix,
$\mathcal{C}(\mX) = \operatorname{span}\cb{(1, 1)}$,
with orthonormal basis $\vecf{q}_1 = \tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\,(1, 1)$.
Then

$$
\matr{Q} \tp{\matr{Q}}
= \tfrac{1}{2} \begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ 1 \end{bmatrix} \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \end{bmatrix}
= \begin{bmatrix} 0.5 & 0.5 \\ 0.5 & 0.5 \end{bmatrix},
$$

the hat matrix found in @exm-hat-matrix.
The fitted values $(\bar{y}, \bar{y})$ are the closest point to $\vy$ on the line of constant vectors
(@thm-closest-point),
and the residuals $(y_1 - \bar{y}, y_2 - \bar{y})$ are orthogonal to $(1, 1)$:
they sum to $0$.

:::
